question: The pair as recorded has no shared question. P-981's RS1/RS2 AUCs (0.640, 0.712) discriminate PREVALENT MCI from normal cognition at baseline, which is detection, not prediction of incident MCI (conditions 1 and 6). But P-981 also prints one incident-MCI estimate, RS3. That one shares P-824's question: predicting incident MCI in Chinese community-dwelling adults from clinical, questionnaire and cognitive data (one channel). The following differences are allowed and recorded as candidate explanations: predictors (P-824 has no cognitive test; RS3 adds MMSE, memory and fluency scores), label definition (single screening-score thresholds against Petersen consensus MCI), horizon (5 years against a mean of about 2 years), cohort, and validation.
metric: ROC AUC on both sides (P-981 equates it with the c statistic).

figures.P-981: RS3, incident MCI, apparent (fitted and scored on the same sub-cohort): AUC 0.785, no interval; 72 converters and 849 stable among 921 normal at baseline. Hanley-McNeil: Q1 = 0.785/1.215 = 0.646, Q2 = 2(0.6162)/1.785 = 0.690, SE = sqrt([0.785(0.215) + 71(0.646-0.616) + 848(0.690-0.616)]/(72*849)) = 0.0327, giving 0.721-0.849. RS1/RS2 (prevalent MCI, not compared): 0.640 (0.620-0.660) and 0.712 (0.694-0.730).
figures.P-824: 5-year AUC with no interval in the text. Hanley-McNeil uses the event counts of Supplementary Table 1 (all follow-up, so an approximation for the 5-year AUC). CHARLS, development: 0.861 with 2323/6470, SE 0.0051, giving 0.851-0.871. CLHLS, external: 0.797 with 862/3819, SE 0.0095, giving 0.778-0.816. RuLAS, external: 0.823 with 260/391, SE 0.0176, giving 0.789-0.857.
figures.comparison: CHARLS against RS3, both apparent estimates: 0.861 lies outside 0.721-0.849 (by 0.012) and 0.785 lies outside 0.851-0.871; z = 0.076/sqrt(0.0051^2 + 0.0327^2) = 2.30. RuLAS against RS3: 0.785 lies outside 0.789-0.857 by 0.004, but 0.823 lies inside RS3's interval; z = 1.02. CLHLS against RS3: each lies inside the other's interval; z = 0.35.

matched_figure_check: No figure under the other's condition is printed. P-824 says its 3-year result 'did not change substantially', which is near P-981's horizon of about 2 years, but the value is only in Supplementary Figure 3, so at the matched horizon P-824 reports no reconciling number. P-981 prints no incident-MCI AUC for its test-free scores: RS1/RS2 were compared with RS3 on the incident sub-cohort only in Supplementary Table S1. The RS1/RS2 AUCs in its text are prevalent-MCI figures. P-824's CLHLS figure (0.797) agrees with 0.785, but it comes from another cohort aged 65+ with another label (CMMSE < 18), not from P-981's condition.
performance_validity: Passes. No figure reaches 0.97; the highest is P-824's CHARLS 0.861 on 8,793 participants with two external cohorts. P-981's 0.785 is apparent on 72 events, so any optimism would lower it.

candidate_explanations.difference: Outcome label: P-824 counts 'incident MCI' from a single screening-score threshold that differs by cohort (1 SD below the mean in CHARLS, CMMSE < 18, HDS < 21.5). P-981 requires a two-expert Petersen consensus with memory-only impairment.
candidate_explanations.quote: a participant was deﬁned to have incident MCI if his or her cognitive score was more than 1 SD below the mean

candidate_explanations.difference: Outcome label (P-981 side): consensus Petersen MCI with objective memory impairment and no impairment in other domains.
candidate_explanations.quote: Consensus diagnoses were assigned by two multidisciplinary experts. The subjects were diagnosed with MCI if they had the following symptoms according to Petersen’s criteria

candidate_explanations.difference: Predictors within the channel: P-824's score is self-reported, with education the strongest term. RS3 adds memory and verbal-fluency test scores to RS2, which already contains MMSE.
candidate_explanations.quote: we added cognitive performance to risk model 3 for predicting incident MCI.

candidate_explanations.difference: Horizon: 5-year AUC against a mean follow-up of about 2 years in P-981's incident sub-cohort.
candidate_explanations.quote: Length of Follow up (y) 2.25 1.86 2.01 1.37 (Table 4: NC-MCI mean, SD; NC-NC mean, SD)

candidate_explanations.difference: Sample size and events: RS3 rests on 72 incident cases in 921 participants, against 2,323 events in P-824's development cohort.
candidate_explanations.quote: At baseline, 921 participants were classiﬁed as normal cognition (NC); among them, 849 participants maintained NC status, and 72 (7.8%) developed MCI.

candidate_explanations.difference: Cohort and age range: CHARLS adults 45+ (mean age 57.9), CLHLS 65+ (mean 80.9) and RuLAS 70-87, against BABRI Beijing adults aged 50-80 with MMSE > 23. P-824's own figures move from 0.861 to 0.797 across cohorts, which its authors attribute to age and missing predictors.
candidate_explanations.quote: Finally, the predictive utility for MCI was relatively low in CLHLS, which may be attributed to the older age of the par- ticipants or the exclusion of other important variables

reason: The record's figures (P-981's RS1/RS2, 0.64-0.70) are prevalent-MCI AUCs, a misreading, and they fail condition 1. The pair is judged on P-981's one incident-MCI estimate (RS3, 0.785). That estimate differs beyond uncertainty from P-824's development-cohort figure (0.861) in both directions (z = 2.30). It lies just outside RuLAS's derived interval in one direction only (by 0.004), and it agrees with P-824's CLHLS validation (0.797). The pair is borderline because it meets condition 4 only against P-824's development cohort, while one of P-824's own external cohorts agrees with P-981. None of the candidate explanations (label definition, predictors, horizon, events, cohort) is shown to be sufficient.

quotes.quote: Our empirical work suggested that the area under the curve for a 5-year MCI prediction was 0.861 in CHARLS, 0.797 in CLHLS, and 0.823 in RuLAS.
We found that when the prediction time changed to 3 or 7 years, the result did not change substantially (Supplementary Figures 3 and 4).
MCI occurred Yes 2323 (26.4) 862 (18.4) 260 (39.9) No 6470 (73.6) 3819 (81.6) 391 (60.1) (Supplementary Table 1: CHARLS n = 8793, CLHLS n = 4681, RuLAS n = 651)
participant was deﬁned to have incident MCI if his or her Hasegawa’s Dementia Scale (HDS) score was less than 21.5 during follow-up.
The AUC of the incident MCI model was 0.785, sensitivity = 0.717, and speciﬁcity = 0.830
The AUC for model 1 was 0.640 (95% CI 0.620–0.660), and the AUC for model 2 was 0.712 (0.694–0.730)
In this sample, 1,174 subjects (19.8%) were diagnosed with MCI.

By comparing the RS1 and RS2 models, we found that RS2 with N1N5 (B = −0.073, p = 0.005), Rodelay (B = −0.072, p = 0.013), and VFT (B = −0.078, p = 0.001) scores had better performance, as shown in Supplementary Table S1.
